text: ## 📋 Summary This PR introduces the `AppSidebar` component, which persists its collapsed/expanded state in `localStorage` and subscribes to state updates using `useSyncExternalStore`. While the subscription mechanics and React hooks usage are clean, reading persistent layout state from `localStorage` in an SSR/Next.js environment introduces unavoidable layout shifts (CLS) on initial load, and collapsed links lack robust accessible names. --- ## 🔍 Findings ### 🟠 High * **`hard_app_sidebar.tsx:20-29`** — **SSR/Client layout shift (CLS/FOUC) from `localStorage` layout persistence** Because `localStorage` is purely client-side, `getServerSnapshot()` must always fall back to `"expanded"`. When a user with a saved `"collapsed"` preference loads an SSR page: 1. The server renders the expanded sidebar HTML. 2. React hydrates the initial `"expanded"` HTML. 3. `useSyncExternalStore` detects `getSnapshot() === "collapsed"` and triggers a post-hydration re-render to collapse the sidebar. This causes a visible Flash of Uncollapsed Content (FOUC) and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) on every initial page load. **Fix**: For layout-critical state in Next.js/SSR, persist the collapse preference in a **cookie** instead of `localStorage`. Read the cookie on the server (e.g., via `cookies()` in Next.js server components or middleware) and pass the initial state into the component/store so the server and client render the exact same initial layout without shifting. --- ### 🟡 Medium * **`hard_app_sidebar.tsx:61-66`** — **Collapsed navigation links lack a reliable accessible name** When `collapsed === true`, `nav-label` is not rendered and `` is hidden from the accessibility tree. The link relies solely on `title={collapsed ? item.label : undefined}` for naming. Relying on `title` as the sole accessible name is an accessibility anti-pattern (WCAG 2.1) because screen reader support for `title` attributes on interactive elements is inconsistent. **Fix**: Always render the label in the DOM, using a visually-hidden (screen-reader only) class when collapsed, or set `aria-label={item.label}` on ``: ```tsx {item.label} ``` --- ### 🟢 Low * **`hard_app_sidebar.tsx:20-24, 36`** — **Unhandled `SecurityError` when `localStorage` is restricted** Direct access to `window.localStorage` can throw a `SecurityError` `DOMException` in restricted environments (e.g., strict privacy modes, sandboxed iframes, or disabled storage). If `getSnapshot()` throws during render, it will crash the React render tree. **Fix**: Wrap `localStorage` access in a `try/catch` fallback: ```ts function getSnapshot(): "collapsed" | "expanded" { if (typeof window === "undefined") return "expanded"; try { return window.localStorage.getItem(KEY) === "1" ? "collapsed" : "expanded"; } catch { return "expanded"; } } ``` --- ## ✅ Positives * Correctly implemented `useSyncExternalStore` with stable module-level callbacks and primitive return values to prevent infinite render loops. * Dispatched a synthetic `StorageEvent` in `toggle()` so same-tab state transitions trigger the `useSyncExternalStore` listener in sync with cross-tab updates. * Clean ARIA attributes on the sidebar collapse toggle button (`aria-label`, `aria-hidden` on icons).
